messages:
Alex: quick FYI — after the kernel-selector change in last deploy I'm seeing a measurable perf regression on TP+PP 8xA100 runs. Nsight capture shows prolonged all-reduce stalls between matmuls.
Maria: details? numbers? :thinking:
Alex: baseline (before change) avg token latency 48ms, p95 92ms. After change avg 62ms, p95 145ms. Throughput down ~18%.
Alex: nvprof snippet from rank0:
```text
GPU activities:
  MatMul      65%  (overlapped)
  AllReduce   28%  (serialized)
Elapsed time for all kernels:  220.12 ms
AllReduce time (sum over calls):  61.4 ms
``` 
Alex: Nsight timeline (short): long idle gaps after each MatMul while NCCL ops wait for completion on other ranks — looks like kernel ordering changed.
Chen: did kernel-selector flip to the new 'AggressiveFusedGemm' path? That changes launch ordering and may break our comm/compute overlap assumptions.
Alex: yes, kernel_selector=aggressive since 1763389000 rollout
Julia: can we repro with synthetic workload in perf-harness? I can run a capture with `--nvtx` and our microbench config.
Sam: repro would help. Also capture per-op custom timers we added last quarter; those give us exact host enqueue vs device start times.
Maria: can you paste the custom-timer dump? Those were supposed to show how much of AllReduce waits for host vs GPU.
Alex: custom timer slice:
```text
[op] MatMul_1 enqueue 0.0ms start 0.2ms end 4.8ms
[op] MatMul_1 finished on GPU 4.8ms
[op] NCCL_AllReduce_1 enqueue 4.85ms start 40.2ms end 61.7ms
-- host->device gap ~35ms
```
Chen: that host->device gap is suspicious; suggests we serialized too much on host before issuing NCCL calls. The aggressive fused gemm might be doing some post-processing on host.
Julia: I can run Nsight with `--trace` and export the API events. If API events show delayed ncclCommEnqueue calls we can blame host-side ordering.
InfraBot: deploy 1763389000 toggled kernel_selector=aggressive into production at 2026-03-16T12:03:20Z
Sam: quick mitigation: roll back kernel-selector to 'balanced' for dedicated clusters, or enable `async-nccl-launch=true` flag to push NCCL launches earlier.
Chen: there is a race if we enable async-nccl-launch without ensuring stream ordering. Need to validate correctness.
Alex: agree. For now I scheduled a perf run on perf-ci group with 8xA100 (TP=2 PP=4) and added NVTX + custom timers. Run id 20260316-PR-482.
Maria: add a short nsight capture too (1000ms window) — we only need the critical section.
Julia: I'll pick this up. If repro is stable I'll instrument the kernel-selector with a barrier to keep previous ordering and rerun to confirm regression root cause.
Alex: thanks. tagging @Chen @Sam for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
Chen: noted, will look into selector code path and host-side post-processing.
Sam: I'll prepare a config to flip `kernel_selector` via feature flag per pool, so we can A/B test without full rollback.
Alex: perfect. if anyone sees strong dev-prod alerts, ping infra channel. closing here when we have nvprof+nsight captures.
InfraBot: perf-ci run 20260316-PR-482 started (ETA ~45m) :eyes:
